name: Vijayanagara Empire
summary: A South Indian Hindu empire whose capital at Hampi was one of the largest cities in the world. It was broken at the Battle of Talikota in 1565.

knownFor.label: Hampi
knownFor.note: The ruined capital, a UNESCO site full of temples and markets.

knownFor.label: Stone Chariot
knownFor.note: A shrine shaped like a chariot at the Vittala Temple.

knownFor.label: Carnatic music
knownFor.note: South Indian classical music took its framework in this era.

knownFor.label: War elephants
knownFor.note: Used in large numbers, including at Talikota.

terrain.value: The Deccan plateau and the Tungabhadra river.

climate.value: Semi-arid on the Deccan plateau; farming depended on the monsoon and on reservoirs.

disasters.value: Droughts, which the empire countered with reservoirs and canals.

urbanisation.value: The capital may have had several hundred thousand people.

migration.value: Unknown in detail; Telugu-speaking warriors and settlers moved south into Tamil lands.

economicBase.value: Irrigated agriculture, supported by state-sponsored canals and reservoirs.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Vijayanagara Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Stein, Vijayanagara (1989)

tradeRoutes.value: Bought war horses from Arab and later Portuguese traders through west-coast ports such as Goa and Bhatkal.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: The varaha (gold coin, called “pagoda” by Europeans); land taxes collected through nayaka governors.

inequality.value: Great wealth in the royal court and temples; foreign visitors described rich markets.

governmentType.value: Monarchy, with nayaka governors holding land for military service.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Vijayanagara Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Stein, Vijayanagara (1989)

keyRulers.value: Harihara I, Bukka Raya I, Deva Raya II, Krishna Deva Raya (1509–1529).

succession.value: Four successive dynasties: Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu.

institutions.value: Nayaka governors held land in return for military service.

stability.value: Collapsed after defeat at Talikota (1565), though the dynasty survived elsewhere.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Vijayanagara Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Stein, Vijayanagara (1989)

eliteConflict.value: Regents such as Rama Raya held real power over the emperors.

armyAndTech.value: Large army with war elephants and imported horses.

majorWars.value: Long wars with the Bahmani and Deccan sultanates, ending in defeat at Talikota (1565).

territoryChange.value: Ruled most of southern India, about 880,000 km² around 1500.

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals of the Deccan sultanates; traded and sometimes allied with the Portuguese.

inventions.value: Water tanks and aqueducts that supplied the capital.

scienceEducation.value: Kerala school of mathematics flourished in the region.

openness.value: Welcomed Portuguese, Persian and Arab traders, especially in horses.

communicationTransport.value: Roads and ports; horses imported by sea; ox carts.

religion.value: Hinduism, with royal patronage of temples (Virupaksha, Vittala).
religion.source: Wikipedia: Vijayanagara Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Stein, Vijayanagara (1989)

languageWriting.value: Kannada, Telugu, Tamil and Sanskrit, all used in literature and inscriptions.

artsArchitecture.value: Huge temple gateways (rajagopurams) and the capital at Hampi, a World Heritage Site.

socialStructure.value: Brahmins, warrior nobles, merchants, artisans and farmers within the caste system.

sharedIdentity.value: Hindu kingship, presented as defending South Indian traditions.

dailyLife.value: Houses of mud and stone; rice, millet, lentils and buttermilk; busy bazaars in Hampi.

neighbours.value: The Bahmani Sultanate, later the Deccan sultanates, Gajapati Odisha and the Portuguese.

ideasReligions.value: Carnatic music took its classical framework; Telugu and Kannada literature flourished.

riseSignals.value: Founded in 1336 by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Vijayanagara Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Stein, Vijayanagara (1989)

peakPeriod.value: Under Krishna Deva Raya (1509–1529), when foreign visitors praised the size of the capital.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Vijayanagara Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Stein, Vijayanagara (1989)

declineSignals.value: Defeat by an alliance of Deccan sultanates at Talikota (1565).
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Vijayanagara Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Stein, Vijayanagara (1989)

outcome.value: The capital was sacked in 1565; the empire moved south and ended in 1646.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Vijayanagara Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Stein, Vijayanagara (1989)

overallCertainty.value: Good. Inscriptions and accounts of Persian and Portuguese visitors.
